There is a pre-existing mixin limitation: TableRowExpandMixin updates a single expandRowLabel on the component. Expanding one row changes the aria-label/title on every expand button in the table. 

The added `:aria-label` in this diff still isn’t row-specific (e.g. “Expand HTTPS Certificate details”).

Event Logs uses separate chevron-up/down icons which is clearer visually.

Fixed. Replaced shared expandRowLabel with expandLabel(row) method
that uses row.detailsShowing and appends the certificate name, e.g.
"Expand table row HTTPS Certificate". Each row now has a unique
aria-label independent of other rows.

There are no tests under tests/unit/ for Certificates. 
Recommendation: Add at least:

- Store mapping test: given a mock Redfish Certificate response, verify issuer, subject, serialNumber, etc. are mapped correctly

- Component test: expand row toggles #row-details, formatSerialNumber behavior, conditional field visibility

This is important for a security-adjacent admin feature.

Added tests/unit/views/SecurityAndAccess/Certificates/:
- CertificatesStore.spec.js: store mapping, Version conversion,
  absent Version, Version=0 edge case, certificateString excluded
- Certificates.spec.js: expandLabel per-row identity,
  formatSerialNumber all input cases
The feature is a solid UX improvement!

inconsistent spacing in the DN abbreviations:

"Issuer Country(C)" → should be "Issuer Country (C)"
Same for (L), (CN), (O), (OU), (ST) across issuer and subject keys
Done

Two problems:

1. Always shown: Because `version` is always truthy (defaults to 3), the expanded view always renders the version row even when the API omitted `Version`.
2. Misleading default: Inventing `3` when the field is absent is incorrect for audit/compliance use cases this feature targets.

Additionally, Redfish/X.509 Version is the ASN.1 integer (e.g. 2 means X.509 v3), not a human-friendly “version 3”. Displaying the raw integer without translation may confuse admins.

Recommendation: Only store/display Version when present. Consider displaying Version + 1 with a label like “X.509 v3”, or omit the field if semantics are unclear.
Done

The full PEM is pulled into Vuex on every certificate load but never rendered or used. That adds memory overhead (PEM strings can be several KB each) and exposes cert material in Vue DevTools without user benefit.

Recommendation: comment out `certificateString` from the store mapping unless a follow-up feature (copy PEM, download, fingerprint) is planned in this CL.
Done

Inventory detail rows use <b-col sm="6"> for a two-column layout that stacks on small screens. Certificates uses bare <b-col>, which stays side-by-side at all breakpoints and may be cramped on narrow viewports.

Recommendation: Match Inventory: `<b-col sm="6">`.
Done

Section headings like “Issuer Information” and “Subject Information” always render, even when every child field is hidden.

On a BMC that only returns CommonName, users see a heading with no fields beneath it (or only one field under a bold section header).

Recommendation: Wrap each <h6> + its fields in a container with a computed/helper that checks whether any field in that section has data, similar to how Inventory avoids empty blocks.

Fixed. Issuer and Subject section headings wrapped in
<template v-if> checking all fields. Heading is hidden when
all fields in the section are absent.

This blindly splits every two characters. Problems:

Input: A1:B2:C3 (already colon-separated)
Result: A1::B2::C3 (broken)
Expected: Pass through unchanged

Input: 1234567890 (decimal string)
Result: 12:34:56:78:90 (misleading)
Expected: Display as-is

Recommendation: Return early if the string already contains :, or only format when the string matches /^[0-9A-Fa-f]+$/. Otherwise display the raw Redfish value.
Done

Approve (+1) — ready to merge from a code perspective.

All prior review feedback has been implemented correctly. Last patch adds solid unit tests, improves accessibility beyond the original ask, and fixes the data-correctness issues (version default, PEM in Vuex, serial formatting). CI passes.

"Certificate Details" / "Validity Period" headings always render

Issuer/Subject headings are conditional; these two are not. If a BMC omits all metadata fields, users could see empty section headers. Unlikely in practice since validFrom/validUntil are always populated.
Done

1234567890 still becomes 12:34:56:78:90 because digits 0–9 are valid hex. 
this is low risk. Optional follow-up: only reformat when length is even and length ≥ 4, or when string contains A–F.
Done

Component tests do not cover:
1. expand/collapse toggling #row-details
2. conditional field visibility in the template

Acceptable for this CL; integration tests could be a follow-up.
Done
